assertions.source: log refuted (−55..−90%); cosh degenerate (|tr|<2); SnapPy braid closures non-hyperbolic (Vol≈0). All derived volumes fail.

description: Derive-or-refute: does B = ρ·[Vol(atom)−Vol(free)] close A≥3 binding, using DERIVED volumes (no census-knot fit)? Three observables all fail: (A) log|tr_M| volume — no derived ρ closes it (−55…−90%); (B) cosh-inversion — every |tr_M|<2 (elliptic), no real length; (C) SnapPy on the derived braid closure — non-hyperbolic (degenerate tetrahedra, Vol≈0). Hyperbolic volume needs complex-q (Kashaev N→∞), absent at the real substrate q₀; the only nonzero volumes come from hand-assigned census knots = a per-isotope fit. Converges with PR #1421 (no derived atom→knot rule).

conclusion.interpretation: hyperbolic volume needs complex-q Kashaev N→∞, absent at real q₀; nonzero vols only via census-knot fit. Linear truncation not repaired by any real-q volume difference — missing structure is in the archimedean (complex-q) step.
